Definition: Audio primarily dominated by an identifiable engine or motor operating as the acoustic source
Examples: Diesel engine; petrol engine; turbine engine; electric motor
Exclusions: Complete vehicle scenes; general machinery without identifiable engine; rotor-dominant audio
Acoustic_Characteristics: Periodic/quasi-periodic components; harmonics; mechanical vibration; tonal and broadband components
Data_Gap: Need verified engine-specific source labels and deployment recordings
Notes: Dataset labels must be verified before inclusion.

Definition: Audio primarily associated with rotating blades, rotors, propellers, or aerodynamic rotating components
Examples: Helicopter rotor; drone rotor; propeller; large rotating fan
Exclusions: Engine-dominant recordings; general machinery; complete vehicle scenes
Acoustic_Characteristics: Blade-passing components; harmonics; tonal/broadband aerodynamic noise; rotational modulation
Data_Gap: Example mapping ESC-50 Helicopter -> Project ROTOR is PARTIAL, not a direct original class equivalence
Notes: Rotor and engine content may coexist.

Definition: Audio representing a vehicle-level acoustic scene rather than a single isolated mechanical component
Examples: Moving vehicle; vehicle pass-by; vehicle interior acoustic environment
Exclusions: Isolated engine recordings; isolated rotor recordings; generic machinery
Acoustic_Characteristics: Engine; drivetrain; tire/road interaction; aerodynamic noise; environmental interaction
Data_Gap: Whole-vehicle versus component-level definition requires empirical validation
Notes: Do not map every engine recording to VEHICLE.

Definition: General mechanical equipment or industrial/mechanical acoustic activity that cannot be more specifically assigned
Examples: Industrial machinery; machine operation; mechanical tools
Exclusions: Clearly identifiable engine-only; rotor-dominant; vehicle-level scenes
Acoustic_Characteristics: Mechanical harmonics; vibration; periodic/quasi-periodic and broadband components
Data_Gap: Broad class; risk of semantic overlap
Notes: Use specific classes when source identity is sufficiently clear.

Definition: Audio primarily caused by wind or aerodynamic airflow
Examples: Strong wind; turbulence; wind passing microphone; outdoor airflow
Exclusions: Rotor-specific aerodynamic noise; vehicle-specific aerodynamic noise; rain-dominated recordings
Acoustic_Characteristics: Broadband low-frequency energy; turbulence; microphone-dependent effects
Notes: Wind may be environmental background rather than discrete event.

Definition: Audio primarily generated by rainfall or precipitation interacting with surfaces/environment
Examples: Light rain; heavy rain; rain on surfaces
Exclusions: Water machinery; wind-dominated recordings; unrelated transient sounds
Acoustic_Characteristics: Broadband transient activity; repeated small impacts; stochastic temporal structure
Notes: Rain can resemble repeated impulsive events.

Definition: Emergency or warning siren with characteristic temporal/spectral modulation
Examples: Emergency vehicle siren; warning siren; air-raid siren
Exclusions: Simple alarm; buzzer; generic tonal signal
Acoustic_Characteristics: Strong tonal components; periodic frequency/amplitude modulation
Data_Gap: Original labels must be verified for siren semantics
Notes: Siren definition must remain distinct from generic alarm.

Definition: Alarm, buzzer, beep, or warning signal that does not meet the specific siren definition
Examples: Electronic alarm; buzzer; warning beep; equipment alarm
Acoustic_Characteristics: Tonal signals; repeated beeps; periodic patterns; narrowband components
Notes: Do not map every warning signal to SIREN.

Definition: Collective human acoustic ambience produced by multiple people rather than clearly identifiable individual speech
Examples: Crowd ambience; stadium crowd; group chatter; public gathering
Exclusions: Clearly identifiable individual speech; isolated voice
Acoustic_Characteristics: Multiple overlapping voices; broadband vocal activity; time-varying energy
Data_Gap: Crowd labels may not correspond directly to project definition
Notes: May be difficult to distinguish from mixed speech/background.

Definition: Short-duration acoustic event characterized by rapid onset and transient energy
Examples: Impact; bang; sudden mechanical strike; sharp transient
Exclusions: Continuous machinery; continuous rain; sirens; alarms
Acoustic_Characteristics: Fast onset; short duration; high peak amplitude; broadband transient energy
Notes: Physical source is less important than temporal structure.

Definition: Human vocal speech intended as spoken communication
Examples: Single-speaker speech; spoken commands; conversation; radio communication
Exclusions: Crowd ambience; non-speech vocal sounds; music
Acoustic_Characteristics: Harmonic vocal structure; formants; time-varying spectral envelope
Data_Gap: Speech preservation is a major deployment requirement
Notes: Should also be used for speech-preservation testing.

Definition: Audio containing multiple simultaneous acoustic sources where single-label assignment loses meaningful information
Data_Gap: Needs multi-label policy and architecture decision
Notes: Do not automatically treat as a conventional single-label class.

Definition: Audio that does not confidently match supported classes or falls outside validated training distribution
Examples: Unseen source; OOD audio; ambiguous audio; low-confidence input
Notes: Prefer rejection mechanism over miscellaneous training bucket.
